title: Transactional config safety and batching recommendation engine
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver an automated, transactionally-applied configuration pipeline that safely evaluates and applies batching and caching recommendations from Redwood Optimize, and provides deterministic automated rollback when economic or correctness guardrails are violated. The system must avoid flapping, keep CPUs/GPUs stable during staged experiments, and integrate with Console rollout controls.

Scope: 1) Recommendation ingestion: accept candidate config bundles (batch sizes, KV cache TTLs, quantization profile) from Optimize or manual sources. 2) Simulated dry-run: run workload simulation against historical traces for cost and latency delta estimation. 3) Transactional staged apply: staged canary/apply with automatic traffic weighting, checkpoint state snapshot, and safe promotion. 4) Automated rollback triggers: guardrails based on latency regressions, error rate, output-quality regression (eval set), and economic thresholds (cost not decreasing by expected margin). 5) State reconciliation: ensure system state converges after failures, support manual-override, and produce a single source-of-truth for current/desired config.

Non-goals: Not covering model architecture changes or kernel-level changes that require model reloads in this ticket. Those will be handled in separate runtime migration work.

Success criteria: measurable cost savings without customer-visible quality regressions, no more than one rolling-back event per 3 months per tenant due to false positives, and clear, auditable changelogs in Console for every applied recommendation.
acceptance_criteria: Can import Optimize recommendations and render delta estimates via simulated dry-run for representative traces
Staged apply executes with snapshot checkpoint and adjustable canary weight; can promote to 100% or revert to snapshot
Automated rollback triggers fire when latency p95 increases by >20% OR 5xx rate increases by >2x OR eval metric regression exceeds threshold configured per model
Dashboard exposes per-recommendation expected vs actual cost delta, and an event trail for applied/reverted config with timestamps and author
State reconciliation recovers to last-known-good config on control-plane restart and surfaces divergence alerts
comments: 2025-02-10 Ava Chen: Initial triage and spec draft. Pulled requirement from PM backlog; Optimize team has a prototype recommender that outputs candidate bundles. Need infra hooks for transactional apply.

2025-02-11 Marcus Patel: Ran early spike to validate snapshot approach using etcd revisions. Snapshot + apply via feature flags looks promising; CPU/GPU transient load is manageable for small canaries.
2025-02-12 Design review: agreed to keep canary window configurable and to include manual approval step for tenant-impacting changes. UX will surface expected cost delta and confidence score.

2025-02-13 Eng review: decided to implement a two-phase canary (1% -> 25% -> 100%) with hysteresis backoff to avoid flip-flop. Added safety fence to block applies when autoscaler events in last 10 minutes touch the same pool.

2025-02-14 PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/9281 implements recommendation ingestion and dry-run simulator harness. Benchmarks attached to PR show median cost delta estimates within 7% of actuals in synthetic traces.
2025-02-15 QA: created synthetic regression tests that inject increased latency and quality drift; automated rollback triggered as expected in 3/3 runs. Next: run on canary tenants in staging.

2025-02-17 Marcus Patel: Blocking item discovered - some legacy deployments lack KV cache instrumentation required by dry-run service. Working with runtime team to add lightweight telemetry shim (ENG-51022).
